chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a runner-up credential from the same regional machine that fed Tropical Mega Battle and Best in Japan. The card is not consolation filler; it is proof of a player landing just below the top of a public tournament route.

claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional second-place source group as one row containing No.2 Trainer at source index 175.
Bulbapedia says No.2 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a second-place prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer iteration was first awarded to the runners-up of each regional Japanese World Challenge Summer event held between July and August 2000, with the circuit split into Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle events.

Bulbapedia says overall winners of the Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented their country in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii, while the remaining top-ranking players competed in a domestic Best in Japan final, both held in late August 2000; this dossier does not treat regional second place as the Hawaii representative slot.

Bulbapedia describes Tropical Mega Battle as an international TCG tournament held annually from 1999 through 2001 at Hilton Hawaiian Village in Honolulu, involving top players from Canada, Latin America, Europe, the United States, and Japan, with about 50 players each year.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference and were Non Holofoil.

Bulbapedia says two base versions of the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer exist, one depicting a male Trainer and the other a female Trainer, with the awarded version depending on the winner's gender.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.2 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Bulbapedia says runners-up of the Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.2 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration, so those final-stage cards must be separated from this non-holo regional second-place class.

Pokumon identifies Boy TMB No.2 Trainer and Girl TMB No.2 Trainer as World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle 2000 regional second-place prizes, Japanese unnumbered non-holo Trainer Winner cards illustrated by Ken Sugimori, and gives estimated copy counts for each gendered version; this dossier treats those counts as collector estimates, not official disclosure.

As judged collector texture, the regional No.2 Trainer matters because it records the near-miss position inside a serious competitive apparatus: not champion, not final-stage photo trophy, but still a named runner-up embedded in the World Challenge Summer route.

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer [World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional]: the runner-up card that still carries the machine
narrative.why_it_matters: No.2 Trainer has a different emotional charge than No.1. It is not the clean champion myth, but it may be more human: a named player, a regional conference, a serious run through the World Challenge Summer structure, and a result close enough to be preserved on a personalized card. The card lets the catalog talk about the people who almost reached the very top, and about how Pokémon's organized play was learning to print rank, route, and memory into cardboard.
not_claiming: that every No.2 Trainer listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.2 Trainer, World Challenge, Tropical Mega Battle, regional second place, TMB, runner-up, male Trainer, female Trainer, personalized name, Best in Japan, or photo trophy.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.2 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the exact route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.2 Trainer / Ｎｏ.２トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional second-place prize, not Secret Super Battle, Best in Japan, 1999 Tropical Mega Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, or World Championships.

Check whether the card is the 2000 World Challenge Summer regional version: non-holo, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male or female Trainer artwork depending on winner gender.

Do not treat regional second place as the same as the Hawaii representative slot. Bulbapedia's Hawaii language belongs to overall winners, while remaining top-ranking players fed into domestic Best in Japan.
Separate this regional non-holo card from Best in Japan final No.2 Trainer cards, which Bulbapedia describes as Holofoil cards with the player's photograph superimposed on the illustration.
Record Pokumon gendered-version copy counts only as collector estimates. Do not convert them into official print-run facts.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including name/conference personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that No.2 Trainer name alone identifies the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer: the near-win made visible
narrative.why_it_matters: No.2 Trainer is where the trophy-card story gets tender. First place is clean mythology; second place is evidence of pressure, skill, and proximity. In this 2000 regional Tropical Mega Battle route, the card carries the runner-up's name and conference, then asks the collector to understand the tournament machine around it. It is not just rare because few exist. It is rare because it preserves a precise human position in a bracket that mostly vanished.
not_claiming: that every No.2 Trainer print follows this route
